target_customer: US Space Force and defense organizations needing maneuverable satellite protection, plus commercial orbital logistics
problem: Satellites cannot maneuver quickly because in-space propulsion is low thrust. Orbital Operations is building a high-thrust, reusable LH2/LOx vehicle with cryogenic management to protect satellites.
business_model: Government contracts and awards (defense), later commercial orbital logistics
product_category: Space propulsion and orbital vehicles for defense

founders.name: Ben Schleuniger
founders.background_notes: YC page: propulsion at NASA, then SpaceX, early employee at Relativity Space owning fluid systems for TM1 and heat exchangers for Aeon R.

founders.name: Ross Doherty
founders.background_notes: YC page: owned turbomachinery manufacturing and assembly for Aeon R and ran flight termination system qualification for TM-1.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reusable high-thrust cryogenic in-space propulsion with a 20 K cryocooler and zero boil-off storage is hardware-intensive and unproven at orbital scale; first demo still pending.

defensibility.rationale: Cryogenic management and propulsion know-how are hard to replicate and defense contracting favors vetted vendors, though capital needs are heavy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well-funded maneuvering and servicing startups were active (Impulse won a Space Force and DIU contract in October 2024 per one search summary). Nothing found showing a competitor copying the cryo high-thrust approach.

market_need_then: Space Force interest in maneuverable and defensive satellites is growing; a SpaceWERX award and an NASA support letter are cited by the company and press.

branding.domain_note: Uses orbitalops.tech (not a .com); acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Logo file referenced, design not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and mission-led: 'Made to move. Designed to defend.'

branding.brand_signature: Mythology-themed product names (Astraeus, Typhon, Boreas) and tagline 'Made to move. Designed to defend.'

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive company name with memorable product names, but no press or community evidence about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Orbital Operations raised an $8.8M seed in August 2025 led by Initialized Capital after YC and reports a SpaceWERX award and a later DoD demo award headline. Founders come from SpaceX, Blue Origin and Relativity. No exit or shutdown was found. The key risk is technical: the cryo vehicle demo and capital for hardware.
notes: Seed confirmed by lead investor blog and Payload Space. One valuation site lists $15.3M total; other sources list $8.8M only, so coverage is partial. A DoD cryogenic demo award (October 2026 headline) and a SpaceWERX award were seen only in secondary or headline form, not recorded as rounds. Competitor pages found were dated 2025 to 2026 or undated, so competition list is empty. A January 2026 profile says the team is two people while the YC page says 10.
